maya: quick heads-up — onboarding rnk-v2-small int8 shows a weird split. MRR on holdout is up ~0.8% but NDCG@10 is down ~1.6%, mostly concentrated on the long-tail queries.
kevin: can you paste the eval command and the exact numbers?
maya: yeah, ran eval on holdout-2025-longtail (10k queries). command:```./eval_rerank --model=rnk-v2-small-int8 --candidate-set=top100 --metric=ndcg,mrr --k=10 --seed=42 --holdout=holdout-2025-longtail```results snippet: NDCG@10: 0.432 -> 0.425 (-1.6%), MRR@10: 0.271 -> 0.273 (+0.8%)
simon: interesting — did you change candidate ordering or de-duping between runs? that often pushes top-1/2 shifts that affect NDCG more than MRR.
maya: no explicit change in dedupe. but noticed that the int8 runtime batching does dynamic candidate shuffling when batchmix>1 to balance latency. could that affect evaluation determinism?
lina: that shuffling would only reorder ties or equal scores, but if quantization narrows score gaps, you might get more ties and different tie-break behavior -> NDCG drop.
kevin: can we repro on single-thread eval (no batchmix) and with stable sort tie-break? also try deterministic topk selection:```--deterministic-sorting --topk-stable```
maya: running now. also going to compare with prod-sampled queries and an alternate holdout with the same candidate retrieval to rule out candidate churn.
eval-bot: job 3509876543-1 started: eval_rerank (deterministic-sorting=false, batchmix=2)
simon: if deterministic run fixes NDCG, we need to change our bring-up checklist: require deterministic evaluation for any quantized candidate-scored models. also add an anchor-sensitivity slice: queries with many near-equal score candidates (top10 score stddev < 0.01).
lina: agreed. add a quick check: compute fraction of queries where top2 score delta < 1e-3 before/after quant. that will highlight score compression.
maya: quick interim results: deterministic run (batchmix=1, --deterministic-sorting) gives NDCG@10: 0.431 -> 0.430 (-0.2%), MRR: +0.7% -> so most of the -1.6% was ordering instability. detailed per-slice followup incoming.
kevin: cool — sounds like two separate effects: quantization compresses scores a bit (small MRR up maybe due to calibration) + batching/order instability amplifies NDCG loss. plan: 1) add deterministic eval to gating, 2) compute anchor-sensitivity slice and add to golden checks, 3) if quant compression too high, try hybrid quant config (activations fp16).
simon: do we have an easy script to produce the anchor-sensitivity slice? if not I can drop a quick one today.
maya: please do. Also flagging product: this could affect SERP ordering for long-tail users; want a short rollout pause until we gate on these checks.
kevin: filing a tiny rollout hold: @product-team FYI — we are pausing rnk-v2-small-int8 canary until deterministic eval & anchor slice pass. :eyes:
maya: thanks — will post the per-query diff sheet once I finish the slice reports.
kevin: thx — loop back when you have the slice CSV (include topk text & scores)
